summary.summary: Brentwood's covering report presents the unaudited (pre-audit) Statement of Accounts 2025/26, certified by the s151 officer as true and fair and published by the 30 June statutory deadline, with the audited version due by 31 January 2027. The statutory public inspection period runs 1 July to 11 August 2026 and had drawn no requests to see documents and no representations to the external auditors at the time of writing. The accounts are prepared on a going-concern basis, resting on the council's reserves and its track record of delivering efficiencies, and the report explicitly states that looming local government reorganisation does not change that view because vesting is beyond the 12-month horizon. The financial statements themselves are Appendix A, a separate document, so this paper carries no balance-sheet figures.

news_drafts.headline: Brentwood's capital spending plan falls 25% behind in first quarter, creating delivery risk
news_drafts.lead: Brentwood council is on track to spend only three-quarters of its planned capital expenditure in the first quarter of 2026/27, with a £13.6 million shortfall against a £54.5 million budget. The underspend masks volatile performance across individual projects. The council's affordable housing programme, budgeted at £37.2 million for the quarter, is forecast to spend only £26.2 million, a 30 per cent slip. Meanwhile, the Baytree project is running at just 20 per cent of its planned £5 million spend. However, two other major projects are overrunning: the Depot Redevelopment faces a £1 million overspend and the Brentwood Centre Redevelopment a £591,000 overspend. The quarterly shortfall raises questions about whether the council can deliver its capital programme on schedule.

findings.headline: Overall capital programme underspent by 25% in Q1, with (£13,573k) variance
findings.detail: The total capital programme shows budgeted spend of £54,548k against a Q1 forecast outturn of £40,975k, a variance of (£13,573k). The council is on track to spend only 75% of planned Q1 capital expenditure.
findings.matters: Capital programme delivery is a key indicator of project management and financial control; a 25% Q1 underspend raises whether the council will meet full-year capital expenditure targets and the implications for financing and cash flow forecasting.

findings.headline: HRA Affordable Housing programme shows 30% Q1 underspend with (£11,018k) variance
findings.detail: The HRA Affordable Housing programme was budgeted at £37,185k for Q1 but is forecast to spend only £26,167k, a significant underspend of (£11,018k) representing 30% of planned Q1 expenditure.
findings.matters: Affordable housing delivery is typically match-funded and subject to grant conditions; substantial underspend suggests delivery delays or programme changes that could affect grant certainty and the council's ability to meet housing commitments.

findings.headline: Brentwood Centre Redevelopment is overrunning, with £591k overspend against £1,409k Q1 budget
findings.detail: The Brentwood Centre Redevelopment was budgeted at £1,409k for Q1 but is forecast to spend £2,000k, a £591k overspend representing a 42% cost overrun on planned Q1 spend.
findings.matters: Major council redevelopment projects showing cost overruns signal project delivery risk and create uncertainty around total project financing and the council's capital position.

findings.headline: Depot Redevelopment is overrunning at more than 100% of Q1 budget, with £1,000k overspend
findings.detail: The Depot Redevelopment project was budgeted at £987k for Q1 but is forecast to spend £1,987k, an overspend of £1,000k. The forecast outturn has doubled the planned Q1 expenditure.
findings.matters: Cost overruns of this scale indicate potential cost control issues or scope drift that could affect the total project outturn and the council's overall capital position, with implications for borrowing requirements.

findings.headline: Baytree project is 80% underspent in Q1, with (£3,979k) variance against £4,979k budget
findings.detail: The Baytree capital project was budgeted at £4,979k for Q1 but is forecast to spend only £1,000k. This represents a variance of (£3,979k), indicating either substantial project delay or delivery disruption.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether capital projects are being delivered on schedule; an 80% underspend in Q1 suggests project delays, capability issues, or funding constraints that could affect the council's ability to spend planned capital and refinance accordingly.
